EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a characteristic carbon-yl doublet at 1821 cm⁻¹ and 1759 cm⁻¹. A high-frequency C=O band above 1800 cm⁻¹ is typical for an acyl halide, especially an acyl fluoride, whose C=O stretch is split by Fermi resonance into a pair near 1820 / 1760 cm⁻¹.  A strong C–F stretching band is expected in the 1000–1100 cm⁻¹ region and is observed at 1015 cm⁻¹, with intense CF bending / deformation bands near 680 cm⁻¹ (peak at 673 cm⁻¹) and around 800 cm⁻¹ (peaks at 810 cm⁻¹ and 788 cm⁻¹).  The prominent C–H stretch at 2946 cm⁻¹ and CH₃/CH₂ bending at 1436 cm⁻¹ and 1374 cm⁻¹ match the propyl chain. Among the candidates, only molecule 2 (CCC(=O)OF) contains an acyl-F functionality together with an aliphatic chain, fitting all of these key Raman features; the other candidates either lack a carbonyl, have the C=O frequency too low, or do not contain fluorine.
